page.layout: One page of text: a running head at the top, then a four-line verse stanza in the upper text block. Below it, a central woodcut emblem with a printed oval inscription and, under the emblem, a printed date line. No page number, catchword or signature.

main_text.l: Non ego dura pati discrimina mille recuso, Dum tua constanti ueor mandata labore. Sed ne deficiam, ne sæuo vincar ab hoste, Tu mihi præstò veni, tu suffice robora fesso.
IACOBVS MYLIVS. CORONAS ANNVM BENIGNITATIS TVA. PSALM. 65.

page.notes: The running head is printed as "PRECATIO" in spaced capitals. The verse stanza is set in italic type; the italics are not marked in the verse because the whole stanza is italic in the scan and the text is read as printed. The oval inscription lies within the woodcut: it is printed text, so it is transcribed, with the inscription's own reference "PSALM. 65." kept as printed. "TVA" is printed without the ligature and is read as shown on the scan. The date line below the emblem is printed with reversed-C numerals, "clɔ. Iɔ. XXCIIII" in the scan, which reads as MDXCIIII (1594); the printed form appears to contain an extra X, so the reading is uncertain and is given without [?] because the letters are legible in context. Faint show-through from the reverse side at the top right and left is not transcribed. The emblem's figures (two putti, flowers, the central shield with a rebus-like device) are decoration and are not transcribed.
